title: Kasa Applied Programming: Ghana-first data projects
description: Work through five practical coding labs. Core Kasa exercises run locally; newer data helpers are marked as experimental.

units.title: Build a market receipt
units.goal: Calculate quantities, line totals and a final receipt using integer pesewas.
units.concept: Currency values should be integers in minor units. Labels and numeric results are separate output lines until we explicitly convert numbers to text.
units.source:
ma rice_price = 1200
ma rice_qty = 3
ma soap_price = 850
ma soap_qty = 2
ma total_pesewas = rice_price * rice_qty + soap_price * soap_qty
ka "TOTAL PESEWAS"
ka total_pesewas
trace: Three bags of rice cost 3 × 1200 = 3600 pesewas.
Two bars of soap cost 2 × 850 = 1700 pesewas.
The receipt totals 5300 pesewas, equivalent to GHS 53.00.
units.task: Change rice_qty to 4 and predict the new amount before running. Add a separate transport fee of 200 pesewas.
acceptance: Total is computed from quantities and unit prices, not entered as a fixed number.
The currency unit is explained; no unsafe floating-point cash calculation.
Predict and record output before pressing Run.
units.check: What happens to the total if the quantity of soap increases by one?
units.answer: The total increases by 850 pesewas, the price of one soap.
units.mode: Core Kasa — runnable in the embedded lesson editor.

units.title: Analyse student marks
units.goal: Use a list, loop and conditions to compute a total, average and pass decision.
units.concept: Loops are reusable reasoning tools for collecting a total. Averages require a non-empty list to avoid division by zero.
units.source:
ma marks = [50, 70, 90]
ma total = 0
ma i = 0
bere_a i < tentɛn(marks)
    ma total = total + marks[i]
    ma i = i + 1
awiei
ma average = total / tentɛn(marks)
ka total
ka average >= 50
trace: The accumulator starts at zero and sums 50, 70 and 90.
There are three marks. Average is 210 divided by 3, giving 70 (stored in average).
The final Boolean uses an explicitly stated hypothetical threshold of 50.
units.task: Replace the third mark with 60. Recalculate the output, then describe what changes. Write a condition to handle an empty list before dividing.
acceptance: Loop index stays within the list's valid indices.
Pass rule is labelled as an example, not a universal school policy.
units.check: Why should an empty list be checked before computing the average?
units.answer: Because dividing by the number of entries would divide by zero when there are no marks.
units.mode: Core Kasa — runnable in the embedded lesson editor.

units.title: Inventory reorder decisions
units.goal: Calculate closing stock and trigger a reorder using a clear boundary.
units.concept: Closing units are beginning units plus receipts minus sales. Reordering at or below a threshold is different from reordering only below it.
units.source:
ma opening = 20
ma received = 10
ma sold = 23
ma closing = opening + received - sold
ka closing
sɛ closing <= 10 a
    ka "REORDER"
anyɛ_saa_a
    ka "STOCK OK"
awiei
trace: Opening plus received stock is 30 units.
Seven is at or below the threshold of 10, so the reorder branch runs.
units.task: Test closing stock of 9, 10 and 11. What extra validation should stop an impossible sale greater than available stock?
acceptance: Inventory is tracked in whole units, not mixed with money.
A negative closing balance is flagged as invalid rather than accepted silently.
units.check: If closing stock is exactly 10, should the example reorder?
units.answer: Yes. The example uses <= 10, so exactly 10 triggers REORDER.
units.mode: Core Kasa — runnable in the embedded lesson editor.

units.title: From lists to tables
units.goal: Understand rows, columns and the distinction between core list code and experimental helpers.
units.concept: A table can be represented as a list of lists. Kasa's G1.4 table helpers are source-only, not shipped as a pinned Studio import. Start with direct list indexing in the ordinary editor.
units.source:
ma sales = [[101, 25], [102, 40], [103, -5]]
ka sales[0][0]
ka sales[1][1]
ma total = 0
ma i = 0
bere_a i < tentɛn(sales)
    ma total = total + sales[i][1]
    ma i = i + 1
awiei
ka total
trace: The second column sums to 60, including the negative adjustment.
units.task: Add a fourth row and update the expected total. What should happen if one row has no second column?
acceptance: Rows and columns are both zero-based.
A short row is identified before indexing column 1.
The experimental table library is described as source-only; no fa tables import is suggested.
units.check: Is fa tables firi stdlib a supported import in the Academy Studio?
units.answer: No. G1.4 table helpers are source-only experimental functions, not part of the pinned G1 import catalog.
units.mode: Core list example runs here; source-only G1.4 helpers are not importable.

units.title: Named fields and validation
units.goal: Explain schema order, required fields and why validating input prevents inaccurate business reports.
units.concept: G1.5 positional records use a separate ordered list of field names. G1.6 typed validation runs in host-side Python/JavaScript adapters, not as a Kasa builtin or Studio mode.
units.source:
ma fields = ["id", "name", "amount"]
ma record = [101, "Ama", 2500]
ka fields[1]
ka record[1]
ka tentɛn(fields) == tentɛn(record)
ka record[2] >= 0
trace: The schema says position 1 represents the name field.
The widths match; amount 2500 minor units is nonnegative.
units.task: Create a second record containing hwee for name. Explain why field presence must not be confused with truthiness and why an external validator should check the record.
acceptance: Schema field order and record position are aligned.
Required null values are identified as invalid inputs.
No JSON import, decimal validation or production safety claim is made.
units.check: Can a learner call G1.6 host validation from ordinary Kasa source?
units.answer: No. It is currently a separate Python/JavaScript host adapter, not an importable language builtin.
units.mode: Core list example runs here; record and typed validation helpers remain experimental.
